clue.text: 10's epitaph: "I died (RIP): Hell hath no bar open the while, a disaster"

definitions.note: the answer to 10 across is the comedian W C Fields, to whom this line is famously attributed as an epitaph

indicators.note: a disaster is a wreck, so the letters of the quoted words before it are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.words: I died (RIP): Hell hath no bar open the while, a

explanation.surface: A quoted gravestone grumble about the afterlife having no open bar, which would be a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' is the anagram signal; every letter from I through to the 'a' before it, that little word included, is shuffled into the eight-word line.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke line about preferring Philadelphia is popularly said to be the gravestone inscription W C Fields wanted.

clue.text: Finished with taking the wheel, too much to handle?

parts.note: something finished is over
to take the wheel is to be at the helm, so helming

explanation.surface: A driver who has finished a long stint at the wheel finds it all too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overwhelming is more than one can cope with, too much to handle.

clue.text: Like Aguecheek with "a lean and hungry look"? In fact, he'd collapsed!

definitions.text: Like Aguecheek with "a lean and hungry look"?

indicators.note: collapsed means fallen in a heap, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Sir Andrew Aguecheek, said to look lean and hungry, has fallen in a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lean and hungry look' is Caesar's line about Cassius, applied here to the skinny Aguecheek of Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean and hungry look describes a gaunt, narrow countenance, which is the meaning of the hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Scots intend to take the lid off the boiler

indicators.note: the lid of a word written down is its top letter, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a kettle is a boiler of water

explanation.surface: A Scottish plan to remove the lid from a boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the K from KETTLE leaves the Scots verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ettle is a Scots and northern dialect verb meaning to purpose or plan.

clue.text: See 1
Closest to one male umpire

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
to umpire a dispute is to mediate in it

explanation.surface: A male umpire standing nearest to the action.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means nearest in time or space, so closest is a synonym.

clue.text: Get up the nose, say, of the Astronomer Royal

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: to get up someone's nose is to annoy or rile them

explanation.surface: Someone annoying the Astronomer Royal by getting up his nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Martin Ryle, the radio astronomer, held the honorary post of Astronomer Royal from 1972 to 1982.

clue.text: Great golfer Eldrick losing final for flooring

indicators.note: losing its final letter means the last letter of the golfer's name is dropped

parts.note: Eldrick is the given name of the golfer known as Tiger Woods

explanation.surface: A golfing great falls in a tournament final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing final' drops the closing S from the golfer's name; the 'flooring' sounds like being knocked down but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigerwood is a striped tropical hardwood often sold as floorboards.

clue.text: Great golfer! That's my girl!

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African major-winning golfer
that is gives i.e., the Latin abbreviation id est

explanation.surface: A proud parent cheering a golfing daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's name, so it can stand for my girl.

clue.text: One deducing knowledge from goose spittle? I'm confused!

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone tries to learn something from goose spit and is baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistemology is the philosophical study of knowledge, so its practitioner reasons about what can be known.

clue.text: See 1 across
Can areas of study define a wit?

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, abbreviated WC for water closet
academic disciplines are fields

explanation.surface: Asking whether academic disciplines can pin down what a wit is.
explanation.definitionFit: W C Fields was an American comic actor celebrated for his barbed one-liners.

clue.text: Behind with the delivery

definitions.meaning: a person's behind is their rump or buttocks
a birth in which the baby arrives bottom first is so called

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the buttocks, and a delivery with the baby's bottom first is named after them.

clue.text: Skin colour's origin's apparent once I speak about it!

parts.note: ex means former, what something once was

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter
about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Someone holding forth on where skin colour comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: To excoriate is to strip or abrade the skin, so skin used as a verb means the same.

clue.text: Failure turning blue with effort can be determined

indicators.note: turning means changing round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a failure is a loser

explanation.surface: A failure going blue in the face with effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with effort' is linking surface: the anagram of LOSER and BLUE gives the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Resoluble means able to be resolved or settled, so something that can be determined.

clue.text: How some buy wine as the negociant's in fear guarding the margin

parts.note: the French for in is en, the wine merchant's language

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding protectively, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the French for fear is peur
a rim is an edge or margin

explanation.surface: A French wine dealer nervous about protecting his profit margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as the negociant's' (a French wine merchant's) tells you to put in and fear into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying en primeur means paying for wine before it is bottled and released, a common way to buy fine Bordeaux.

clue.text: BT Call-minder?

parts.note: BT's Call Minder is an answering service, but read as the body that minded British Telecom it means the old telecoms regulator

explanation.definitionFit: Oftel was the UK Office of Telecommunications, the regulator that oversaw BT before Ofcom replaced it.

clue.text: How far might swordsman go? Oh, the wicked insertion during joust

indicators.note: one piece is inserted during the other, placed inside it

parts.note: to tilt is to joust with a lance

indicators.note: wicked means twisted or bad, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swordsman's daring thrust in the middle of a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' is the anagram signal on 'Oh, the', and 'insertion during' places the result inside the jousting verb; a sword driven in to its hilt is the image.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade plunged in to the hilt goes as far as it can, the idiom for completely.

clue.text: … or could he put his finger on it?

definitions.text: … or could he put his finger on it?

parts.words: … or could he put his finger on it?
parts.note: following the sword going in all the way, this asks who else could touch something and turn it to gold

explanation.definitionFit: King Midas of Greek myth had the gift that everything he touched turned to gold.

clue.text: Smoothed the way old priest worked over

parts.note: ex means former or old
a text that has been worked over has been edited

explanation.surface: A former priest who has been reworked and revised.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite something is to speed it along by removing obstacles, smoothing its way.

clue.text: One with an eye for a poor camel?

definitions.text: One with an eye for a poor camel?

parts.words: One with an eye for a poor camel?
parts.note: alludes to the saying that a camel passes through this thing's eye more easily than a rich man enters heaven

explanation.definitionFit: A sewing tool has an eye, the hole a camel must squeeze through in the Gospel saying.

clue.text: Pathogenic agent could pass through every intestine initially

indicators.note: one piece passes through the other, sitting inside it
initially means the first letters of the words named

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A germ that might travel through any gut.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a gut bacterium, some strains of which cause serious food poisoning.

clue.text: Eye of a VIP

definitions.meaning: the London Eye is a giant observation wheel
a very important person is a bigwig

explanation.definitionFit: A Ferris-type wheel like the London Eye is one sense, and an important person is the slang other.

clue.text: See 1 across
See 1 across
Callow, hogtied, shy. Oh, that is awkward!

parts.note: hogtied means hobbled, tied by the legs

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so these letters are put in a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: Someone tied up, shy and embarrassed by an awkward moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' is the anagram signal on shy, Oh and the abbreviation for 'that is'; a hobbledehoy is an old word for a gawky adolescent boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbledehoy is a clumsy youth, so the adjective means gauche and inexperienced, like callow.

clue.text: Coming from Danzig (EU), nervous traveller

indicators.note: Coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nervous traveller arriving from Danzig in the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Zigeuner is the German word for a Romani person, traditionally seen as a traveller.

clue.text: Run outside!

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run scored without the bat, such as a bye
Latin for outside, as in extramural

explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a run scored in cricket, and the Latin preposition extra means outside or beyond.
